purpose.intro: Some things a caller must have settled before authorization is even worth evaluating — a verified identifier, a required session factor, mandatory profile data, legal consent. The gate holds those obligations in one place: every protected request passes it first, a blocked caller always knows the single next thing to resolve, and no obligation check leaks into services or the frontend.

claims.text: The gate evaluates the caller's obligations — verified identifier, session factor, required profile data, legal consent — and returns clear or unmet. It never resolves queries.
Requirements classify as persistent (facts an account carries — e.g. verified email) or session-based (e.g. re-verify OTP this session).

Unmet requirements resolve one at a time, in fixed order. The wire carries the full set — HTTP **428** with `{ obligations }` in that order — and the resolution page renders only the first, advancing as each clears.
The gate runs **before** scoped AC: an unmet requirement short-circuits with 428 before any AC-governed query executes.
Account-level security requirements (e.g. 2FA) evaluate across **all** memberships, not just the active org — switching org can't bypass them.

Frontend contract: every signed-in page is gated; on a 428, redirect automatically to the resolution page (`/resolve`) — the single page exemption, where each obligation resolves in place. Never leave the user stuck on the failed action. Server-side, only the endpoints that clear obligations stay excluded from the gate.
